story.see: Across the Ararat Valley, towns, ponds and fields share the radar image. Some dry slopes return a weak echo and can look like water. We use elevation to screen dark patches on steep or high ground. Individual ponds and fields remain difficult to track consistently.
story.physics: A preview pixel is roughly 180 metres wide. Our open-water layer finds well under one square kilometre (about 0.3) on every pass, which is probably too little: the comparison with historical water shows that many small water bodies are missed.
story.lband: From Masis toward Vedi, the radar echo can change with wet soil, crops and surface roughness. The cross-polarized channel looks odd on 6 October, probably an instrument or processing effect rather than rain, so we leave it out of change detection. Interferometric coherence (the Coherence layer) does see the farming season that brightness misses: about 43–44 % of the valley floor is incoherent in June–July, 22–25 % by late September–October. Calibrated images and dated ground observations would be needed to test specific field changes.
story.people: Farms and fish ponds in the valley use artesian groundwater. The US Geological Survey found that the area with flowing wells fell from 619 to 291 square kilometres between 1984 and 2016. Ponds are mostly too small for our 180 m pixels, so this map cannot follow them. Well readings tell us about groundwater.
